quick_english: Now the sixteenth chapter: after scripture-based knowing, reasoned meditation arises; the Lord lists divine qualities beginning with fearlessness.
cite_parts: bodhaśca nāma śrutimayajñānānantaraṃ  idamittham-ityevaṃbhūtayukticintābhāvanāmayajñānodayena  vicāravimarśaparāmarśādirūpeṇa  vijātīyanyakkāravirahitatadbhāvanāmayasvabhyastākāravijñānalāb  he sati bhavati
tatra śrutimaye jñāne guruśāstre eva prādhānyena  prabhavataḥ
yukticintābhāvanāmaye tu vimarśakṣamatā  asādhāraṇā śiṣyaguṇasaṃpat pradhānabhūtā
ityabhiprāyeṇa vakṣyamāṇaṃ  vimṛśyaivam-iti vākyaṃ saviṣayaṃ kartuṃ  parikarabandhayojanābhiprāyeṇāha bhagavānguruḥ-   śrībhagavānuvāca   abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ

quick_english: Non-harm, truth, non-anger, renunciation, non-attachment, non-slander, compassion, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and non-restlessness.
Energy, patience, steadfastness, contentment, non-malice, and absence of excessive pride are the divine wealth of one born divine, Bharata.
Hypocrisy, pride, egoism, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the demonic wealth, Partha.
Divine wealth liberates, demonic wealth binds; Arjuna is born divine, so he should not grieve.
cite_parts: sā pravṛddhayā  divyāṃśagrāhiṇyā vidyayā bādhyate iti vastusvabhāva eṣaḥ
tasmādāntarīṃ mohalakṣaṇāmavidyāṃ vihāya  vāhyāvidyātmaśatruhananalakṣaṇaṃ śāstrīyavyāpāram  anutiṣṭha-ityadhyāyārambhaḥ

quick_english: In this world there are two creature-creations, divine and demonic; the divine was spoken in detail, now hear the demonic, Partha.
cite_parts: dvau bhūtasargau loke'smin daiva āsura eva ca
daivo vistarataḥ  prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu

quick_english: This divine wealth is described by abhaya and so on; demonic people do not know activity or cessation, and purity, conduct, and truth are not found in them.
cite_parts: āsurīmāha   pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ
na śaucaṃ nāpi  cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate

quick_english: They call the world untrue, unstable, lordless, and causeless; they see no effect beyond what is seen.
cite_parts: na kiṃcit dṛṣṭādanyat kāryaṃ vidyate yatreti-akiṃcitkam

quick_english: Relying on this view, lost selves with small intellects arise as fierce actors, inauspicious for the world's destruction.
Relying on insatiable desire, filled with pride, conceit, and intoxication, they act cruelly with impure vows.
Relying on immeasurable anxiety until dissolution, making desire-enjoyment supreme, they are certain only this much exists.
Bound by hundreds of hope-nooses and devoted to desire and anger, they strive unjustly to gather wealth for desire-enjoyment; their anxiety continues until transmigration and dissolution cease.
cite_parts: etāvaditi-kāmopabhoga eva paraṃ kṛtyaṃ tannāśācca paraṃ  krodhaḥ

quick_english: Today I have gained this; I shall obtain this desire; this is mine and this too; wealth will be mine again.
That enemy was slain by me; I will slay others too; I am lord, enjoyer, accomplished, strong, and happy.
I am wealthy and of noble birth; who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, give, and rejoice; thus they are deluded by ignorance.

Many-minded and confused, gone under delusion's control, attached to sense enjoyments, they fall into impure hell; lacking certainty, they fall into hell beginning with avīci, in the continuum of birth and death.
Self-conceited, stiff, filled with wealth, pride, and intoxication, they sacrifice by name, with hypocrisy and without rule.

Resorting to egoism, strength, pride, desire, and anger, hating the Lord in self and other bodies, they sacrifice by name; such sacrifices do not fruit, and hating worlds they hate the Lord, who is Vasudeva, the all-dwelling.
cite_parts: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ
nāmārthaṃ-prasiddhyarthaṃ ye yajñāḥ  yena yajñayājyayam-iti vyapadeśo jāyate

quick_english: I continually cast those hateful cruel lowest men into asuri wombs.

tokens.grounds: fused verb and locative phrase with indeed

quick_english: Born in asuri wombs, deluded ones fail to reach me and go to the lowest state; hating ones act harmfully and cause hell-fall, so I cast them into asuri wombs.
cite_parts: ātmani ca dveṣavantaḥ ātmano hyahitaṃ nirayapātahetumācaranti

quick_english: Desire, anger, and greed are the threefold gate of hell and destruction of self; therefore one should abandon this triad.
cite_parts: yataḥ kāmādikaṃ trayaṃ narakasyaiva dvāram tasmādetattyajet

quick_english: Freed from these three dark gates, O Kaunteya, a man practices for self and then goes to the supreme destination.

This is not a human saying to disregard; scripture here is beginningless authority. One who abandons scriptural rule and acts from desire attains neither perfection, happiness, nor supreme destination.
cite_parts: na caitat puruṣavacanamityanādaraṇīyam apitu anādi śāstramatra  pramāṇam-ityucyate   yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ
na sa  siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim

quick_english: Therefore scripture is authority for you in determining action and inaction; having known this, you should do scripturally prescribed action here. Abandoning scriptural rule and deliberating by one's own opinion leads to fall into hell, so do not determine action and inaction by self-intellect; this is the purport.
cite_parts: śāstravidhiṃ tyajataḥ svamanīṣayaiva kāryākāryavicāraṃ  kurvataḥ pratyuta narakapātaḥ

label: 16-sangraha
quick_english: In ignorance, one should not determine duty by one's own intellect; rather, by the rule declared in scripture, and scripture itself increases knowing. Thus ends the sixteenth chapter of Abhinavagupta's Gathering of the Gita's Meaning.
cite_parts: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   abodhe svātmabuddhyaiva kāryaṃ naiva vicārayet
